reviews.title: This app makes no sense
reviews.text:
This app is fine at letting you pay your rent online. Cool, it does the one thing it sets out to. However, the account management behind the app has been by far the worst I have ever encountered. “See all your leases, past, present, and future in one app.” Okay, if that’s the truth, why does it allow me to make two separate accounts using the same email? Now, I am locked out of my current lease’s resident portal and am unable to log into my upcoming lease’s resident portal. My assumption is that is due to the fact that it allowed me to create a new account using the same email, and now it’s all a mess.

Viewing that event in the light most favorable to this app, that still doesn’t explain why it never remembers my password. 

I set one password at the beginning. My phone auto populates my email and password upon login to RP. App says that my email/password is incorrect. Try that again a few times. Still not letting me log in. Okay, I’ll just change my password real quick. I change my password. RP tells me that my password is successfully changed. I go back to log in to my portal using the password I just created. “Invalid credentials. Please try again.” 

That has happened about 5 times in one year. It’s ridiculous that something so simple as account creation is totally and completely broken

reviews.title: Policy violation - extra fees
reviews.text:
I paid rent via a resident portal app using Apple Pay. On the review screen every charge showed a dollar amount and a Grand Total. Next to “Convenience Fee” it only said “Calculated in next step” — no amount was displayed.
There was no next step. The app went straight to the Apple Pay confirmation. Because the fee was never shown, I assumed there was none and authorized the payment. I was later charged an extra $50 I never saw or agreed to.
Also, the “Add New” payment button sits very close to the payment-method dropdown. I accidentally opened the dropdown instead of adding a new method; it still showed no fee, so I proceeded thinking I had selected Add New.
The lack of a visible fee amount before authorization is misleading.

reviews.title: Payment Interface Flaw
reviews.text: First, the portal is OK with certain functions like maintenance requests, and seeing messages from the landlord. That’s about it with the pros! On to the CONS of the portal especially when it comes to payment processing. In my situation I split the rent with someone else who also has their payment account in the portal. The problem comes down to when you switch from one payment account to the other, AND edit the dollar amount. When you use the drop down menu for your payment accounts and select a different account, then enter a different dollar amount and click save it would appear initially that you have chosen the payment account you want to use since it’s the only one that now appears on the payment submit screen. HOWEVER, you have to check the circle again in order for it to be used. In my case, I clicked Submit Payment and the wrong payment account was used by defaulting to the previous account. This resulted in me having to pay an $85 NSF fee. So, if you plan on using the payment portal with multiple payment accounts then be sure to click the circle twice. Once on the drop down menu, and again on the payment submit screen. The property manager refused to refund the fee, and claims no responsibility. This was my experience, and going forward I would highly recommend using money orders instead of technology in my opinion.

reviews.title: Malicious fees
reviews.text: Make sure to avoid using this app to make rent payments at all costs. About half of the times I have had to use this app my payments have suspiciously been declined, even though there has not been an issue with the accounts I connected. I have deliberately been charged very high NSF fees on multiple occasions, and after consistently trying to reach out to customer support and other staff members, I have been ignored. I have resorted to paying my rent through checks. The software is maliciously designed to charge you sneaky fees despite trying to make payments in full and ahead of time. And the customer service agents will consistently inform you that they do not deal with individual residents and that they only deal with management officers because those are their direct clients. I repeat do not use this app.
